chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd and Safwan ibn Yahya from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"It is permissible to sacrifice the males of camels and cattle in the provinces if they do not find the females, and the females are superior." As for those other than camels and cattle, the male is [permissible]."

key_terms.اَلْفَحْلُ: the male (specifically of sheep/goats or general male animal)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sacrifice male camels or cattle if females are not available?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of animal sacrifice by establishing a hierarchy of preference: while female camels and cattle are superior, males are legally permissible (ja'iz) in their absence. It further generalizes this permissibility to other livestock, affirming that males are valid for sacrifice when females are not available, reflecting the practical flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding ritual slaughter.
